Missing material includes applicable Part A factors, footnote 2 and the remaining requirements in paragraphs 10–13. No external dependency IDs are supplied. Actual responsibilities, appointments, supervision, performance, incidents, remediation and assessment period also remain unspecified; absence of these facts must not become a false result.

Paragraph 14 places the express request qualification before demonstration and requires demonstration to the SFC's satisfaction. Footnote 5 supplies minimum content; its independently unqualified wording leaves a rival reading requiring resolution. Neither reading makes absence of an SFC request proof of substantive compliance.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 concern distinct request-conditioned procurement duties: audit or verification, and a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. Neither procurement nor absence of a request establishes fulfillment of paragraph 10.

The intermediary due-diligence and controls provisions in the final source unit have their own actor and activity conditions. They cannot silently supply a universal Product Provider supervision standard.

Outsourcing is expressly prevented from displacing responsibility; it is not an exception permitting reduced responsibility. Conversely, retained responsibility does not expressly prohibit delegation or require personal performance of every task.

Preserve SHOULD modality. The excerpts establish neither strict liability for every incident nor a safe harbor based solely on diligent supervision, formal authority, an audit or an allocation of register-maintenance duties.
